h: Ryedale Days to Pair With the Park
p: Kirby Misperton sits in the Vale of Pickering, a wide, flat valley between the North York Moors and the Howardian Hills, so the park is surrounded by some brilliant days out.

Eden Camp in Malton is a museum set in a real Second World War prisoner-of-war camp, with each hut telling a different part of the story of the war. It's genuinely gripping for older children and grown-ups alike. Castle Howard, a few miles west of Malton, is one of the grandest stately homes in England, with lakes, gardens, an adventure playground and the house famously used in Brideshead Revisited.

Pickering, just north of the park, is the southern terminus of the North Yorkshire Moors Railway, where steam trains climb up through Newtondale to Goathland and on towards Whitby. Goathland station was Hogsmeade in the first Harry Potter film, which delights young wizards. Dalby Forest, north-east of Pickering, has mountain bike trails, walking routes and Go Ape, ideal for an active day.

For the park itself, eat early or late to avoid the lunchtime crush, and save the zoo areas for the hottest part of the day when ride queues peak. Bring a refillable bottle and sun cream in summer, and a full set of waterproofs if the forecast looks iffy, as the rides and the zoo are both mainly outdoors. It makes the whole area a cracking base for a family week.
